name: The Content Engine: 12 Prompts for Solo Founders
tagline: Turn a single business insight into a full week of high-converting social posts and newsletters.
metaDescription: Transform one idea into seven days of strategic content. 12 plug-and-play prompts tailored for solo founders building authority on social and newsletters.
description:
The Content Engine is built specifically for solo founders who need consistent organic distribution without spending twenty hours a week drafting posts. When you are managing product development, customer support, and sales, marketing often gets pushed aside.

This prompt pack solves content fatigue by extracting an entire week of multi-channel publishing from a single core insight. Whether your seed idea is a recent customer support ticket, a product pivot, or a technical failure, these 12 prompts guide your AI model to unpack it into diverse, engaging formats.

These prompts avoid generic marketing jargon. Instead, they enforce founder-led positioning: tactical teardowns, contrarian perspective shifts, data-backed case studies, and relatable build-in-public stories. Each prompt includes structural constraints, tone guardrails, and practical usage tips to ensure the output sounds like an authentic operator, not a generic marketing agency. Stop wondering what to write every morning and build an automated distribution workflow.
includes: 12 structured prompts formatted for Claude, ChatGPT, and open models
Markdown (.md) and PDF formats for quick reference
Prompt modification checklist for brand voice calibration
sampleItems: Take this core insight: [INSERT INSIGHT]. Write a vulnerable, high-signal LinkedIn post about a recent obstacle I faced while building my product around this theme. Structure: 1) The hook highlighting the friction, 2) The actual cost or mistake, 3) The specific fix implemented, 4) The tactical lesson for other founders. Keep sentences punchy and conversational. Avoid corporate jargon and fake vulnerability. Usage tip: Provide raw numbers (e.g., hours lost, churn percentage) in your input to make the generated story immediately credible.

Using this topic: [INSERT TOPIC], draft a contrarian thought-leadership post for LinkedIn and X. Identify the common 'best practice' that most founders follow regarding this issue, then argue why that advice is broken for bootstrapped or solo operators. Present an alternative, resource-efficient approach based on my experience. Structure it with a provocative opening statement, three supporting arguments, and a closing question. Usage tip: Specify the exact bad advice you want to debunk before running the prompt.

items.title: The Raw Behind-the-Scenes Teardown
items.body: Take this core insight: [INSERT INSIGHT]. Write a vulnerable, high-signal LinkedIn post about a recent obstacle I faced while building my product around this theme. Structure: 1) The hook highlighting the friction, 2) The actual cost or mistake, 3) The specific fix implemented, 4) The tactical lesson for other founders. Keep sentences punchy and conversational. Avoid corporate jargon and fake vulnerability. Usage tip: Provide raw numbers (e.g., hours lost, churn percentage) in your input to make the generated story immediately credible.

items.title: The Contrarian Take on Industry Advice
items.body: Using this topic: [INSERT TOPIC], draft a contrarian thought-leadership post for LinkedIn and X. Identify the common 'best practice' that most founders follow regarding this issue, then argue why that advice is broken for bootstrapped or solo operators. Present an alternative, resource-efficient approach based on my experience. Structure it with a provocative opening statement, three supporting arguments, and a closing question. Usage tip: Specify the exact bad advice you want to debunk before running the prompt.

items.title: The Step-by-Step Tactical Framework
items.body: Transform this concept: [INSERT CONCEPT] into an actionable, step-by-step educational guide for solo operators. Break the concept down into 3 to 4 sequential, highly actionable steps. For each step, include: What to do, What tool or tactic to use, and a common mistake to avoid. Format this with clean bullet points and clear subheaders optimized for high readability. Usage tip: Paste your rough notes directly into the prompt without formatting—the prompt will handle logical organization.

items.title: The Customer Conversation Transformation
items.body: Based on this customer interaction: [INSERT NOTES/QUOTE], generate a story-driven social post illustrating customer pain and resolution. Protect anonymity. Structure: 1) The direct quote or dilemma the customer shared, 2) Why traditional solutions failed them, 3) How our specific process or product solved it, 4) A universal takeaway for operators. Tone should be empathetic, analytical, and humble. Usage tip: Use this to demonstrate deep customer empathy rather than aggressively pitching your product features directly.

items.title: The Punchy 5-Part X Thread
items.body: Condense this core theme: [INSERT THEME] into a high-engagement 5-tweet thread for X. Tweet 1: A compelling hook promising a clear ROI. Tweets 2-4: Three standalone insights, each delivering an immediately actionable tip. Tweet 5: A summary takeaway with a soft invitation to reply or follow. Tone: Authoritative, concise, no fluff or filler emojis. Usage tip: Run this prompt after drafting your long-form post to extract the sharpest, most viral soundbites automatically.

items.title: The Weekly Founder Newsletter Dispatch
items.body: Turn this central topic: [INSERT TOPIC] into a 300-word founder newsletter entry. Structure: 1) Subject line options (one curiosity-driven, one benefit-driven), 2) A personal check-in bridging my weekly reality to the topic, 3) The core thesis explained simply, 4) Three bulleted takeaways, 5) A direct question to prompt subscriber replies. Keep the tone intimate and peer-to-peer. Usage tip: Include one candid personal observation about your work week in the prompt input to increase reader connection.

items.title: The Old Way vs. New Way Comparison
items.body: Using this theme: [INSERT THEME], construct a visual text comparison contrasting the legacy approach with the modern solo-founder approach. Format as two distinct columns or clean bullet groups: 'The Old Way (Slow, Expensive, Manual)' versus 'The New Way (Lean, Automated, Focused)'. Follow the list with a two-sentence synthesis explaining why speed wins. Usage tip: Pair this generated text with a simple screenshot or 2x2 matrix graphic to double engagement on platforms like LinkedIn.

items.title: The Curated Resource & Tool Stack
items.body: Develop a high-value resource curation post around this problem: [INSERT PROBLEM]. Present 4 practical tools, templates, or workflows that solve this issue for resource-constrained founders. For each item, state: The tool/resource name, Exactly what it replaces, and The specific workflow benefit. End with a question asking the audience for their recommendations. Usage tip: Insert your own product or free template as item #3 to organically weave your offer into high-utility content.

items.title: The Problem-Agitate-Solve Conversion Post
items.body: Write a high-converting social post focused on this pain point: [INSERT PAIN POINT]. Apply the PAS (Problem-Agitate-Solve) copywriting framework tailored for founders. Clearly articulate the frustration, quantify the hidden time or revenue loss, and position my solution [INSERT PRODUCT/SERVICE] as the streamlined answer. End with a clear, low-friction call to action (e.g., link in comments). Usage tip: Use this prompt once per week toward the end of your content cycle to drive direct conversions.

items.title: The Mythbuster Teardown
items.body: Target this widely accepted industry assumption: [INSERT ASSUMPTION]. Generate a rigorous teardown explaining why this assumption is actively costing solo founders time or money. Provide: 1) The popular myth, 2) Real-world operational context showing why it fails, 3) A simpler rule of thumb to use instead. Ensure the argument relies on practical founder logic rather than academic theory. Usage tip: Pick an assumption your prospective customers frequently voice during discovery calls for maximum resonance.

items.title: The Community Q&A Synthesis
items.body: Address this common question I receive from peers or users: [INSERT QUESTION]. Craft a clear, direct-answer post. Format: 1) State the question clearly in the hook, 2) Provide the direct 1-sentence answer upfront, 3) Detail the 3 underlying reasons behind the answer, 4) Provide an immediate implementation checklist. Close by inviting readers to drop their follow-up questions below. Usage tip: Keep a running list of questions from social DMs and customer emails to feed this prompt.

items.title: The 30-Day Experiment Retrospective
items.body: Analyze this recent internal experiment or workflow change: [INSERT EXPERIMENT DETAILS]. Create an analytical retrospective post for founders. Outline: The hypothesis tested, The timeframe and constraints, The quantitative and qualitative results, and The ultimate verdict (Keep, Kill, or Modify). Tone must be objective, analytical, and humble. Usage tip: Even failed experiments make fantastic authority-building posts—input your raw negative metrics without hesitation to stand out from hype-driven accounts.
